gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-traditional-: Disorder draws its curves straight into the stems with no swelling, and its tall lowercase looks oversized on the line. Noto Traditional Nushu follows in a broad-nibbed sans stroke.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-numans: Numans is the quiet one here, a modern sans with widely spaced letters. Disorder takes the big sizes, so try it large and let Numans stay modest beneath it.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-onest: Disorder has a raw, scratchy edge, since its curves meet stems without any swelling and its lowercase looks oversized. Onest is a plain sans with short ascenders and gentle lines, so paragraphs would go down smoothly.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-open-sans: Raw and jittery, Disorder keeps every curve as thin as a drawn thread from start to finish. Open Sans gives it a smooth, sturdy counterpart, so the page gets noise first and then relief.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-orienta: Scrappy and spaced out, Disorder looks like wire bent into letters, thin and uniform throughout. Orienta steps in with a modern sans whose open counters feel like a breath after all that wire.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-oxygen: Oxygen reads as a clean sans-serif, with open curves and a lowercase that nearly matches its capitals. And Disorder, with curves that never thin at the turns, supplies the jagged energy above it.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-parkinsans: Chaotic and loose, Disorder spreads its big-looking lowercase well apart. Parkinsans holds one stroke thickness throughout as a plain sans, and its wide-mouthed letters stay crisp even when shrunk.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-pathway-extreme: Pathway Extreme is a clean, modern sans with stubby ascenders and descenders beside a big x-height. Disorder is the better shouter, a thread of ink with no taper, while Pathway Extreme is the better talker.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-preahvihear: Rough, spaced and restless, Disorder outlines every letter in one steady thickness. Preahvihear then opens its mouths wide as a sans with a lofty x-height, which gives the page somewhere to rest.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-prompt: Chaotic is the right word for Disorder, with no thin hairline against any thick stem and a lowercase that looks oversized. Prompt, an approachable sans with open apertures, settles the page right after.
